effects.prompt: Discard a card or destroy the top card of your deck?

_comment:
'When this attacks, you may discard a card OR destroy the top card of your deck. If THAT CARD has watery grave, this gets go again.'

The shape is burly_bones_blue's, which reads the same sentence with a different payoff.

THE TWO HALVES OF THE CHOICE HAVE TO STORE THE SAME REF, because 'that card' means whichever one the player actually moved -- so the discard records it and the deck branch LOOKs first and destroys what it looked at. Destroying the top card without looking would leave nothing to ask about, and re-reading the graveyard afterwards would find every card put there this turn rather than this one.

'watery grave' is spelled as the printed text does; REF_HAS_KEYWORD normalises, so the card DB's 'WateryGrave' answers.

THE PRINTED GO AGAIN IS WITHDRAWN. The card DB lists GoAgain unconditionally because it flattens the sentence, so without the card-level declaration the gate is decoration and the attack has go again whether or not a watery-grave card was found. angry_bones prints no keyword and needs no declaration -- adding one there would take away something the card has.
